title.narrative: Pathways to Learning and Recovery: Strengthening Education and Resilience in Homs and Hama- Envelopes 1 and 2

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project "Pathways to Learning and Recovery: Strengthening Education and Resilience in Homs and Hama" aims to deliver comprehensive, integrated humanitarian assistance focused on education, early recovery, livelihoods, and multipurpose cash assistance (MPCA) to vulnerable displaced populations, host communities, and returnees across selected areas in Homs and Hama Governorates, specifically targeting Al-Qusayr, Farqalas, and Ziyara subdistricts. This 12-month project aligns closely with the SHF 2025 First Standard Allocation strategic priorities and contributes directly to humanitarian and resilience-building objectives defined within Envelopes 1 and 2. In line with both Envelopes, the project aims to sustain dignified equitable access to essential services and livelihoods, reduce acute needs, minimize risks and improve the overall living conditions in areas of origin and settlement locations through Back-to-Learning (BTL) campaigns reaching 500 out of school children (260 girls, 240 boys, including 10 children with disabilities) accompanied by their care givers reaching 100 adults, Non-Formal Education programme reaching 2300 children, providing remedial ,catch-up classes, and comprehensive Self Learning programmes designed to reintegrate out-of-school children into formal education in addition to special classes offered to newly returnees to overcome educational interruption. Rehabilitation of education infrastructure will support safe, dignified return and access to education services. This includes the rehabilitation of 44 classrooms with accessibility features, gender-sensitive and disability-accessible WASH facilities, and the installation of three solar energy systems to enable uninterrupted schooling. Complementary activities include intensive teacher professional development for 40 teachers (26 female, 14 male) encompassing Education in Emergencies (EiE), pedagogical practices, and psychosocial support (PSS), coupled with the provision of essential learning materials and school kits benefiting 2,300 children (6-17 years: 1,310 girls, 990 boys), in addition to protection-related awareness sessions linked to topics identified during needs assessment, such mine risks and child labor. Eight hundred out-of-school or language-barrier children will attend two cycles over six months, and 1,500 at-risk children will be split into two cycles of 750 each. Each cycle will use 50 classrooms, with a maximum of 31 students per classroom. Additionally, Parent-Teacher Associations (PTA) will be established in each location to foster community engagement and oversight. Early Recovery and Livelihoods (ERL) activities will focus on improving access to needed resources to reduce reliance on negative coping mechanisms mainly linked with child labor and children dropping out of school, while protecting assets and livelihoods. This will be achieved by creating 75 short-term job opportunities using cash-for-work modality, offering immediate income support to meet basic needs, with 40% targeting female headed HHs. Financial grants to 90 beneficiaries, 36 of whom will be female, will sustain and expand MSMEs, enhancing local economic resilience and employment opportunities. Inclusive community recovery planning practices will be implemented to enhance communities' collective thinking and identify their needs and priorities, with three plans implemented across three locations, addressing ERL-related challenges for approximately 700 people. Multipurpose cash assistance will be provided to 300 vulnerable households, with 25% focus on female-headed households, over a six-month period, informed by needs assessments and coordinated with the Cash Working Group, ensuring vulnerable populations can meet basic essential needs effectively. ltbrgtOverall, the project employs an integrated, multisectoral approach and applies IASC Gender and Age Marker (4) with 5% disability inclusion target and implement do-no harms approaches throughout. ltbrgtlt/pgt
